### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **16** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in assertAudienceConfig; a string literal in resolveEmailVerificationRequirement; a string literal in resolveNoSignInAccountReport; a string literal in start))_
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in assertAudienceConfig; a string literal in resolveEmailVerificationRequirement; a string literal in resolveNoSignInAccountReport; a string literal in start), invite_only (literal, a string literal in assertAudienceConfig), requireEmailVerification (literal, a string literal in applyConfigPatch))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/auth-service.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via AuthManager (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx`  _(via getPublicConfig (symbol, a method of class AuthManager), requireEmailVerification (literal, a string literal in applyConfigPatch))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via email_domain (literal, a string literal in assertAudienceConfig; a string literal in resolveEmailVerificationRequirement; a string literal in resolveNoSignInAccountReport; a string literal in start), invite_only (literal, a string literal in assertAudienceConfig), requireEmailVerification (literal, a string literal in applyConfigPatch))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx`  _(via invite_only (literal, a string literal in assertAudienceConfig))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dcd3bceaa068fc3cfb589bd6e04cd0b89b660580` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `29219d95a5aa07c543bab721357562b7b9de4b61` — the merge of head `e2d18233c99e2bfbd4067aea327801aa8d14afe5` into base `dcd3bceaa068fc3cfb589bd6e04cd0b89b660580`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 29219d95a5aa07c543bab721357562b7b9de4b61 && git checkout 29219d95a5aa07c543bab721357562b7b9de4b61
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin dcd3bceaa068fc3cfb589bd6e04cd0b89b660580 e2d18233c99e2bfbd4067aea327801aa8d14afe5 && git checkout -B drift-repro dcd3bceaa068fc3cfb589bd6e04cd0b89b660580 && git merge --no-ff e2d18233c99e2bfbd4067aea327801aa8d14afe5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json dcd3bceaa068fc3cfb589bd6e04cd0b89b660580
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs dcd3bceaa068fc3cfb589bd6e04cd0b89b660580` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e2d18233c99e2bfbd4067aea327801aa8d14afe5`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs: card #20389 body and its 3 comments (claim, os-dev-report, ACCEPT); PR #20406 body, 11-file list, and the net diff `main...e2d18233c9` (merge-base `db74b169dc`, 11 files, +537/−72); the 39 check-runs on the head — 34 success, 5 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending. Head files read for the hunks' context only: `auth-plugin.ts`, `auth-manager.ts`, `audience-posture.ts`, `index.ts`, and the four docs pages the drift bot named. Nothing built, run or re-run.

Accept-set changes (config entry, `assertAudienceConfig`, and both of its callers):

1. `open` + explicit `requireEmailVerification: false` declared by the deployment (constructor config; host `applyConfigPatch` with the default declarant; settings binding with source `env`) — was refused, now accepted. RIGHT: ruling item 1, and the maintainer's verbatim instruction is an env-variable switch. The env override reaches the manager only through `applySettings` → `applyConfigPatch` (auth-plugin.ts 1488-1492 applies `require_email_verification` only when explicit; 1700-1708 maps source `env` to `deployment`), so "constructor only" would have left `OS_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false` inert.
2. `open` + explicit `false` stored through the settings console (any explicit non-`env` source) — still refused, with the new message `posture 'open' FORCES email verification on unless the DEPLOYMENT turns it off …`, which prescribes the env variable or the stack config. RIGHT: narrower than a literal reading of item 1, but inside its stated scope (the deployment's configuration) and its stated reason (a no-mail pre-production deployment); the console is the one runtime-mutable, agent-writable door and the ruling never named it. The refusal is loud and carries the remedy.
3. `email_domain` + explicit `false`, from every declarant — refused; the message is byte-identical to `main` (the `${posture}` interpolation and the four message fragments are unchanged, the `fail` prefix `[audience] invalid audience configuration:` at audience-posture.ts 238-240 is untouched). RIGHT: ruling item 2, and the acceptance's "same code and message family".
4. `invite_only` — the resolver returns `declared ?? false`; entry validation never reaches the self-registration branch. No change. RIGHT.
5. `open` + absent or `true` — the resolver returns `true`; wiring and advertisement stay forced on (pinned by a control). RIGHT: ruling item 1, second sentence.
6. The declarant bit `deploymentDeclaredVerificationOff` in `AuthManager`: set by the constructor; re-declared only by a patch that carries the `requireEmailVerification` key from the deployment; a console patch leaves it as it stood. `emailAndPassword` is deep-merged in `applyConfigPatch` (auth-manager.ts 4177-4184), so a deployment patch that omits the key cannot strand the bit against a vanished value. A console-stored `false` under `invite_only` followed by a posture switch to `open` is refused (pinned). RIGHT.
7. Wiring: `createAuthInstance` and `getPublicConfig()` both read `resolveEmailVerificationRequirement(posture, declared)`; the wiring still emits nothing when nothing is declared under `invite_only`, so the pre-#20389 better-auth options for that posture are unchanged. RIGHT: ruling item 3, second clause — the advertisement cannot disagree with the behaviour.
8. Warning: one `ctx.logger.warn(OPEN_POSTURE_VERIFICATION_OFF_WARNING)` inside the `kernel:ready` hook (auth-plugin.ts 728-745), after the memoized `ensureAuthSettingsBound`, reading the same advertisement the login UI reads. The text names the posture and both consequences (an unowned address registered and signed in at once; an organization invitation to that address acceptable by that account). A repeated settings pass does not warn again (pinned). RIGHT: ruling item 3, first clause.
9. No-mail-transport boot `error`: under `email_domain` it no longer prescribes `OS_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION=false`, the value that posture refuses; elsewhere it still offers it. RIGHT: message text only, no `email_domain` semantics moved, inside the claimed file, pinned both ways.
10. `resolveNoSignInAccountReport` recovery text gains "unless an 'open' deployment has itself declared it off". RIGHT: its docblock requires agreement with `self-hosting.mdx`, which the same diff amends.

Public-surface changes:

11. `@objectstack/plugin-auth`: `AuthManager.applyConfigPatch(patch, options?)` gains an optional `{ requireEmailVerificationFrom?: 'deployment' | 'console' }` defaulting to `deployment` — additive; every existing call keeps its meaning (host code is the deployment). `assertAudienceConfig` gains an optional third argument, and `resolveEmailVerificationRequirement`, `VerificationDeclarant` and `OPEN_POSTURE_VERIFICATION_OFF_WARNING` are new module exports; `index.ts` does not re-export `audience-posture.js`, so they stay package-internal. RIGHT, and the changeset names the one public widening.
12. `@objectstack/spec`: the `AudienceConfigSchema.posture` `.describe()` text and two docblocks; no shape, default, enum or refinement moved. `content/docs/references/system/auth-config.mdx` is regenerated and both occurrences match the new describe string verbatim. RIGHT: ruling item 4.
13. Docs: `self-hosting.mdx` (new "Email verification under each posture" section; the widening paragraph qualified) and `environment-variables.mdx` (the variable's row). A code search on `main` for the invariant's phrasing under `content/docs` returns exactly these two pages plus the generated reference — all amended. The four further pages the drift bot named (auth-service, services-checklist, authentication, sso) were read at the head and none states the invariant; the two release-owned pages are untouched. RIGHT.
14. Tests: the `open` refusal pins are flipped, not deleted. `audience-posture.test.ts`: entry honoured from the deployment and refused from the console with the new first sentence asserted; the `email_domain` message family for three declarants; the constructor both ways; four `applyConfigPatch` cases; the resolver truth table; an end-of-chain sign-up over the memory engine that mints a session with `user.emailVerified: false`, plus its undeclared control that mints none. `audience-posture-setting.test.ts`: env `false` honoured with exactly one warning and none on a second pass; both doors agreeing while `session_expiry_days` still applies; `email_domain` + env `false` refused with the unchanged message; the boot-error remedy under both postures; two no-warning controls. The one retained refusal (`open` + console-stored `false`) asserts the NEW message, so it is flipped to the built behaviour rather than left as the old pin. RIGHT.
15. Card acceptance, line by line: open + false boots, sign-up yields a session, public config reports false, warning once — pinned; open + absent/true forced — pinned; email_domain + false refused, same family — pinned; invite_only unchanged — pinned; docblock and docs amended — in the diff. All met. The out-of-scope line held: no cloud wiring, no `email_domain` or `invite_only` semantics moved.

Gates on the head: every derived family is a success check-run — Check Changeset (both triggers), Part-of PR must not also close its card, The card this PR closes must claim this branch, single-writer path, Lint & Repo Gates, Test Core 1-6, the five Type Check lanes, Build Core, Build Docs, Check Documentation Links, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate 1-3 and Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Flag docs affected. Skipped: Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), and the duplicate Auto Label / Check PR Size triggers — none is a verdict on this diff. `mergeable_state` is clean.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/20389-open-posture-verification-optout.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`. Matches the diff: plugin-auth widens its accept-set (a config that refused the boot on `main` now boots) and widens one public signature, and refuses nothing it accepted before — minor, neither major nor patch. spec publishes description text only — patch. `Clause-②: yes` is line 3 of the PR body and is in the changeset, as the claim declared; Check Changeset is success on the head. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations:

- Zone-2 item 3 falsified (the settings door carries the maintainer's variable) → built declarant-keyed (option B). Answered by the ACCEPT comment; judged RIGHT here independently, on the code read in ①.1-2 and the measured route of the env override.
- One settings-channel pin retained as a refusal (console-stored `false` under `open`) — RIGHT under B; it asserts the new message.
- In-place fix of the no-mail error text under `email_domain` — RIGHT (①.9).
- Spec `.describe()` string, regenerated reference page, and the `boot-sign-in-reachability.ts` qualifier — RIGHT (①.10, ①.12), inside the claimed surfaces.
- Process items (worktree tracking flag, gate derivation without path args, log location, writes as `hotlong`, `main` not merged before opening, changeset line alignment, report fields, commit trailers) — no contract effect. CI ran on the merge of the head into `main` (`29219d95a5`), which covers the unmerged `main`.

Dev open questions:

- Q1, the console door: B (deployment-declared only), answered by the PM as accepted — judged RIGHT. A would open an agent-writable runtime door the ruling did not name; C was falsified by measurement.
- Q2, the invitation consequence: A (a sentence in the warning, the docs and the changeset), answered — judged RIGHT. The exposure widens a pre-existing carve-out (`requireEmailVerificationOnInvitation: false` is unconditional today), and invitation acceptance is outside the ruling.

Out-of-scope findings:

- `bindAuthSettings` applies the whole auth settings pass in one try, so any refused key silently drops its siblings at `warn` (class a, measured on `main`). Pre-existing; this PR removes the open + env trigger. ESCALATED by the PM to the maintainer because no fleet identity is available here to file a card. It still needs a carrier card.
- `service-settings` auth manifest help text and its i18n bundles, and `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/identity-auth.json` knownGaps, still state the old invariant. Outside the claim's file surface, correctly stopped on. ESCALATED: a one-line follow-up card is needed so the console does not contradict an env-locked `false` row beside it.
- macOS-host-only spec test failures and the `pnpm -s` refusal — host facts; CI on Linux is green. No action.

Observation, within the ruling, not escalated: the warning is boot-time as ruled. A deployment that declares `false` under `invite_only` (legal; the default posture) and later has its posture switched to `open` from the console will honour the standing opt-out (the bit is the deployment's) and advertise `false`, but will not warn until the next boot. The ruling asks for one boot-time warning, and the posture switch is the operator's own logged act.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20389-open-posture-verification-optout`
Reviewed-by: `session_d8bf7d34-4f31-407d-ac85-6cb849eec4bf`

**VERDICT: PASS**
